newsitem.title: USA: Chicago biz leaders drop bid for 2008 Olympics.
newsitem.headline: Chicago biz leaders drop bid for 2008 Olympics.

text.p: A Chicago area business group on Thursday recommended dropping a bid for the city to host the 2008 Summer Olympics.

The task force, which has been studying the economic feasibility of pursuing the games since December, recommended that the city notify the U.S. Olympic Committee of its interest in bidding to host the Summer games in 2012, when they are expected to return to North America.

Citing input from the USOC, the task force determined that the $15 million price tag for preparing a bid, and the "slim chance" that any U.S. city would host the games in 2008, were factors in electing to pursue it later, said Jerry Pearlman, former chairman of Zenith Electronics and the executive director of the task force.
